summary: The declared authority/privacy contract is stronger than the current universal-worker validator. Current code blocks explicit self-promotion labels and known forbidden authority_class values, but it does not cryptographically or structurally bind worker-supplied claim write_scope to the canonical queue opportunity, and it contains no equivalent public-artifact privacy guard. These are canary hardening gaps, not evidence that a protected owner has already been mutated or private data has already leaked.

declared_contract_evidence.finding: Runtime coordinates only; Current/Catalog/Lineage/Human Accepted/Served retain existing owners. Public compilation forbids private transcripts, private Patent snapshots, credentials, LOCAL context and token-gated user data.
Candidate != Human Accepted != Served; public worker/network artifacts must not contain private transcripts, Patent payloads, LOCAL context, credentials or access tokens.
This is a concrete authority owner carrying HUMAN_ACCEPTED/SERVED/current pointers and therefore a useful protected-owner falsification target.

runtime_implementation_evidence.finding: validateClaim checks identity/state fields but does not require claim.write_scope to equal or be a subset of the canonical opportunity.write_scope.
validateUniversalWorkerEnvelope validates attempted_paths against claim.write_scope first, falling back to opportunity.write_scope only when claim.write_scope is absent.
validateAuthorityBoundary rejects explicit CURRENT/HUMAN_ACCEPTED/SERVED self-promotion and a short forbidden authority-class set, but has no independent protected-owner path policy.
CLI validates the envelope supplied by the caller; it does not resolve opportunity_id back to a trusted queue source or verify a canonical opportunity hash/ref itself.
Tests cover out-of-scope writes relative to an ordinary opportunity and forbidden authority_class, but do not cover claim scope escalation or privacy leakage into a public return.

findings.title: Worker-controlled claim scope can become the validator's effective mutation authority
findings.condition: A worker/caller supplies a claim.write_scope broader than the canonical opportunity.write_scope while keeping opportunity_id aligned.
findings.effect: validateClaim does not reject the broadened scope; validateUniversalWorkerEnvelope then validates attempted_paths against claim.write_scope. If upstream mutation tooling treats this report as the gate, the worker can self-expand the scope without changing authority_class.

falsification_case.current_code_path_result: No invariant shown in the inspected validator rejects this solely because claim scope exceeds canonical opportunity scope; scope validation prefers claim.write_scope.
falsification_case.safety_note: This is a static executable-path falsification of the validator contract, not evidence that CURRENT_GRAPH has actually been overwritten.

findings.title: Canonical opportunity provenance is not independently bound by the CLI validator
findings.effect: A forged or stale envelope can present a benign opportunity_id/authority_class plus broadened scopes unless another trusted caller already resolved and froze canonical queue evidence. The validator itself does not provide that trust boundary.
findings.required_property: Validation must consume a trusted opportunity_ref/hash or resolve opportunity_id from the active queue snapshot and fail closed on mismatch/staleness.

findings.title: Public-artifact privacy policy is declarative but not enforced by the universal-worker envelope validator
findings.condition: A return/public evidence artifact contains private transcript text, LOCAL content, credentials/access tokens, Patent payloads or token-gated user data while avoiding forbidden authority labels.
findings.effect: The inspected envelope path has no privacy/provenance validation step comparable to validateAuthorityBoundary or validateMutationScope.
findings.required_property: Public returns need explicit privacy/source labels and a fail-closed publication guard before persistence; secret/private detection should complement, not replace, provenance classification.

findings.title: Authority value recursion conflates reporting existing authority with self-promotion
findings.condition: A critic/evidence artifact truthfully quotes an existing state using exact string values such as SERVED or HUMAN_ACCEPTED.
findings.effect: recurseAuthority may reject evidence merely for containing an authority state string, which can encourage lossy workarounds or weaken auditability.
findings.required_property: Separate asserted_target_authority from observed/evidence authority; forbid mutation/promotion claims, not accurate typed observations.

protected_invariants: Universal workers cannot derive global Current/Human Accepted/Served authority from their own envelope, claim or return.
Claim write scope is never stronger than the canonical opportunity write scope.
Protected authority owners remain blocked independently of worker-supplied metadata.
Public coordination artifacts fail closed on private/LOCAL/secret-bearing provenance.
Observed authority evidence remains reportable without being interpreted as requested promotion.

implementation: Resolve canonical opportunity from a trusted active-queue ref/hash inside the validation boundary; reject caller-supplied mismatch.
Require claim.write_scope to be absent-and-derived or exact/subset of canonical opportunity.write_scope; validate claim authority fields against canonical opportunity too.
Add protected authority-owner path classes independent of opportunity metadata, derived from durable owner/authority registry rather than a worker-editable claim.
Add public-artifact privacy/provenance validator and negative fixtures for private transcript, LOCAL context, credentials/tokens and token-gated data.
Change authority validator to distinguish observed authority facts from requested target authority/promotion.
falsification_tests: claim scope escalation to state/CURRENT_GRAPH.json must fail
forged envelope opportunity scope broader than trusted queue ref must fail
benign authority_class plus protected-owner attempted path must fail
public return carrying privacy_class=LOCAL/private source must fail
public return with credential/token fixture must fail
critic evidence that observes state=SERVED without requesting promotion must pass

dedup_and_coordination.active_overlap: O-SWARM-KERNEL-IMPLEMENT-V1 owns the current universal worker kernel/validator implementation scope and had no durable RETURN at the audit check, so this critic must not concurrently patch those files.

next_work_proposal.activation: After current kernel implementation return is durable and dispositioned, unless that return already closes AUTH-01/AUTH-02/PRIV-01 with tests.
next_work_proposal.mission: Harden canonical opportunity binding, claim scope derivation/subset checks, protected-owner path enforcement and public-artifact privacy validation; add negative tests and an independent verifier.
